newsitem.title: USA: Futures industry officials praise common clearing.
newsitem.headline: Futures industry officials praise common clearing.

text.p: Futures industry officials praised efforts to pursue common clearing between the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and the Chicago Board of Trade and said a common venture was key to fighting cost pressures.

Members of the Joint Strategic Initiatives Committee (JSIC), which the exchanges formed in January 1996, met at the Futures Industry Association conference here and said they were committed to finding ways to consolidate and integrate parts of the Chicago exchanges to save costs.
The joint committee formed a special subcommittee in February to pursue discussions of common clearing in Chicago.
"We think we could provide serious savings to the industry," CBOT chairman Pat Arbor said at a JSIC panel discussion here.
No target date has yet been set for a common clearing project, but exchange officials and futures commission merchants said talks would continue.
The first part of a study commissioned by the committee showed that hardware sharing by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and the Chicago Board of Trade might not give the exchanges a cost advantage.

Chris Hehmeyer, chairman of the Board of Trade Clearing Corporation (BOTCC), said he supported continuing with the second and third parts of the study to gauge the overall feasibility of sharing clearing operations, and he reiterated the BOTCC's full support of common clearing. The BOTCC is the clearing arm of the CBOT.
"We're probably three to four or 10 years late already," warned Larry Mollner, FIA chairman. He said the committee was dedicated to pursuing common Chicago initiatives "in a timely fashion."
CME chairman Jack Sandner said "there is a definite march to common clearing" in Chicago and said the world futures industry was also inevitably leaning toward consolidation to fight growing costs.
